dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) training exercise using indexed file I/O, SCREEN SECTION, COMP-X, and ACCEPT/DISPLAY extensions typical of GnuCOBOL on Linux/Windows
evidence: SCREEN SECTION with blank screen, line/column clauses

purpose.domain_detail: COBOL training exercise (Treinamento Cobol, 2012) for a simple customer registration (cadastro de clientes) system
purpose.summary: A menu-driven batch/interactive program for managing a customer file (cadastro de clientes). It supports adding/updating, deleting, and printing a report of customer records from an indexed sequential file. Written as a training exercise by Jackson R Wippel at HBSIS Informática in 2012.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with blank screen and line/column display
ACCEPT ... FROM ESCAPE KEY for function key handling
88-level condition names for keyboard function keys (F1, F4-F10, PgUp, PgDn)
Indexed file I/O with START/READ NEXT loop
CALL/CANCEL of external report printing subprogram
STRING verb to build dynamic report filename from time
4 COPY statements for screen layouts and file descriptors
Latin-1 box-drawing characters in SCREEN SECTION
verdict.notes: Decoded as latin-1 due to Portuguese characters (ã, Ä box-drawing). Program-id is cadcli (cadastro de clientes). The author comment confirms this is a 2012 COBOL training exercise. One line exceeds 72 columns (comment line at column 7 with *>=== separator). Dialect is most likely GnuCOBOL given COMP-X, SCREEN SECTION style, and ACCEPT FROM ESCAPE KEY.
